title: Workload-aware batching defaults: beta/GA launch plan (tiers + rollout + comms)
creator: Aditya Rao
project: Cost Optimization Automation: Workload-aware batching defaults
description:
Objective
- Launch workload-aware batching defaults via three SLO tiers (fast / standard / cost-efficient) in a way that is safe-by-default, observable, and customer-comprehensible.
- Ship an end-to-end launch plan that coordinates Runtime + SRE + Evals + DevEx + Console, and aligns with Optimize roadmap and messaging.

Scope of this ticket
- Define milestones and go/no-go gates from internal dogfood → limited beta → staged rollout → GA.
- Define beta cohort (accounts, models/regions, eligibility, success criteria).
- Comms checklist: release notes, docs, SDK snippets, Console affordances, internal enablement, and customer-facing opt-in guidance.
- Make sure this does not conflict with existing explicit batching configs (tier is additive + precedence rules are clear).

Out of scope
- Tier parameter selection itself (owned by ENG-18421 + runtime PRs)
- Quality gate implementation details (owned by ENG-18428)

Milestones (proposed)
Phase 0 — Launch readiness definition (W07)
- [PM] Finalize tier contract + customer-facing names + short copy (dependency: PM-413)
- [SRE] Finalize SLO targets/measurement windows + alerting approach per tier (dependency: ENG-18427)
- [Runtime] Confirm supported routes (chat/completions/embeddings), and streaming guardrails for fast tier
Deliverable: Launch checklist + beta cohort list + opt-in/out mechanics

Phase 1 — Internal dogfood behind flag (W08–W09)
- Feature flag present and wired for Hosted + Dedicated; Private config path at least validated in staging
- Metrics landed: queue delay, batch formation stats, per-stage latency + dashboards draft
- Perf canary coverage includes the three tiers across top 3 models and top 2 GPU SKUs
Go/No-Go #1 criteria
- No p95 regressions > 5% for standard tier on baseline workloads vs current defaults (same model/SKU)
- Fast tier passes streaming cadence checks (no sustained token cadence degradation; see streaming regression test)
- No increase in error rate (timeouts/cancels) in internal dogfood > 0.1pp

Phase 2 — Limited beta (W10)
- Enable standard tier for a limited subset (models/regions) with 0–10% traffic ramp; opt-in for fast/cost-efficient
- Run weekly review of dashboards + A/B evaluation summary (quality gate + perf)
Go/No-Go #2 criteria (beta)
- Standard tier: p95 latency within target range for the chosen SLO definition in >= 2 regions
- Cost-efficient tier: measurable unit-econ improvement on target workloads (goal: 10–20% lower $/1M tokens on non-streaming routes) with no unacceptable timeout increase
- Supportability: CS/SE have a troubleshooting playbook and “effective config” is visible (Console or API)

Phase 3 — Staged rollout (W11–W12)
- Ramp standard tier default on selected models/regions to 25% → 50% → 100% (gated by SRE sign-off)
- Keep fast + cost-efficient as explicit opt-in during beta; consider default changes only after sustained stability
Go/No-Go #3 criteria (GA readiness)
- Two weeks of stable metrics at ≥50% traffic for standard tier default
- No open P0/P1 issues on tier selection, precedence, or observability
- Docs + SDK examples merged and published; release notes approved

Phase 4 — GA (target: W12 / runtime-1.21)
- Declare tiered batching defaults generally available for Hosted + Dedicated
- Private: GA if migration notes + helm/installer confirmed; otherwise “available” with explicit version requirements and upgrade notes
- Post-GA: backlog for model-family / GPU-SKU tuning and expanded regions

Beta cohort definition (initial)
Cohort goals
- Represent 3 archetypes: (1) latency-sensitive streaming chat, (2) standard product traffic, (3) cost-optimized batch/non-streaming.
- Include at least one Dedicated or Private-adjacent workflow to validate config propagation and auditability.

Candidate accounts (proposed)
- VertexWave (evaluation): strong cost reduction objective, will opt into cost-efficient on selected routes; requires clear latency tier contract.
- LuminaAI (POC): wants per-route tier selection and dashboards/alerts during pilot; good candidate for “standard” default + fast tier for a subset.
- Internal dogfood: Redwood Console + internal agents workloads (owned by Runtime/SRE) to catch tail latency and overload edge cases early.

Eligibility / guardrails
- Must be on supported models/regions list for beta (to be finalized with Runtime/SRE; avoid long-context variants initially if not benchmarked)
- Opt-in required for cost-efficient tier during beta
- If customer has explicit batching knobs configured today, do not override them; tier is ignored unless explicitly set (or unless we ship a clear migration path)

Success criteria by customer archetype
- Streaming chat (fast tier): stable token cadence + p95 within fast SLO; no “bursty” streaming reported in app traces
- Standard product traffic (standard tier): p95 stable/improved, no increase in cancel/timeout, GPU util trend acceptable
- Cost-optimized batch (cost-efficient tier): 10–20% $/1M tokens reduction on targeted workloads, with error rate within agreed budget

Rollout mechanics (Hosted)
- Feature flag: percentage-based enablement by model+region, with ability to carve out specific customer orgs for beta
- Default behavior (beta): keep existing behavior unless tier is set OR standard tier is enabled-by-default for a limited set (to be decided at Go/No-Go #2)
- Auto-rollback signals (owned by SRE + Evals, but tracked here):
  - p95 latency regression vs baseline > threshold for 10+ min (threshold TBD by tier)
  - timeout rate > threshold for 10+ min
  - elevated queue delay p99 sustained + correlated with cancellation spikes

Rollout mechanics (Dedicated)
- Offer as a config option in deployment templates; provide recommended tier per workload
- Encourage “standard” as default for general purpose; “fast” only when streaming/UX requires
- Ensure there is a clear “effective config” view for Dedicated operators (Console + API)

Rollout mechanics (Private)
- If runtime-1.21 lands with migration support, ship helm/installer value to set tier and keep explicit knobs working
- Provide upgrade notes + validation checklist (smoke test + dashboard verification)

Comms checklist
External/customer-facing
- Docs: “Batching profiles (tiers)” page with (a) what it is, (b) when to use each tier, (c) streaming caveats, (d) how overrides interact, (e) troubleshooting
- SDK snippets: Python/TS/Go examples showing batching_tier usage; include one example of overriding a knob while keeping tier
- Release notes (beta): supported models/regions, known limitations, opt-in/out, and what telemetry to watch
- Console: tier dropdown + short explainer; link to docs; show effective config (resolved tier + overrides)

Internal enablement
- #support + #solutions-engineering: 1-pager on when to recommend each tier + common failure modes
- On-call: rollout plan + dashboards to watch + rollback owner and steps
- Sales/SE: positioning guidance aligned with Optimize (emphasize predictable trade-offs; avoid “free savings” claim)

Alignment with Optimize roadmap
- This launch is the first “safe-by-default” cost/perf automation step for Optimize; messaging should reinforce:
  - Customers get predictable behavior via tiers before bespoke tuning
  - Observability and explainability are part of the product (effective config + per-tier dashboards)
  - We will follow with model-family tuning and optional recommendations surfaced in Optimize (Phase 4+ backlog)

Open questions (need answers for Go/No-Go #1)
1) Final customer-facing names: do we keep “cost-efficient” or shorten to “eco” in UI? Current leaning: keep “cost-efficient” for clarity.
2) What is the exact tier SLO contract (p95/p99 targets and windows) per route type (streaming vs non-streaming)? Owned by SRE doc; tracked here for launch sign-off.
3) Which models/regions are in the first beta allowlist? Need Runtime + SRE to propose based on perf-canary coverage.
4) Can we guarantee an “effective config” surface by beta (Console or API endpoint)? This is a launch blocker given early support feedback.

Links / artifacts (to be attached)
- Confluence PRD + design spec + ADR for tiered batching profiles
- Drive: beta cohort planning doc + rollout checklist
- GitHub: runtime-1.21 PRs for tier schema, metrics, perf canary, effective config explain endpoint

Risks to call out in beta invite
- Tail latency/queue delay sensitivity for streaming; fast tier may trade off throughput
- Model-family variance; tier defaults may change by model/SKU over time (we will version and document changes)
- Overload behavior: cost-efficient tier may increase queueing under high concurrency; must rely on overload protection and clear error budgets

Definition of done (for PM-412)
- Milestones and gates agreed by Product + Runtime + SRE + Evals + DevEx in a single shared plan
- Beta cohort confirmed with named accounts + internal dogfood owners
- Comms checklist completed with owners and dates (docs, release notes, Console, SDK examples, enablement)
- Rollout plan includes abort conditions + rollback owner + monitoring checklist
- Alignment statement with Optimize roadmap and positioning approved by Product + DevEx

2025-02-26 (Monica Patel): SDK updates can ship without breaking API, but we need stable naming. Please confirm final enum values (fast/standard/cost_efficient vs cost-efficient).

2025-03-03 (Rafael Mendes): Rollout requirement: must have automated rollback hooks wired to p95 + timeout regressions before we enable defaults beyond 10%. Added as Go/No-Go #2 requirement; will coordinate with release train.

2025-03-06 (Aditya Rao): Updated due date to align with runtime-1.21 branch cut. Next action: finalize beta allowlist (models/regions) with Runtime after perf-canary results, and lock comms owners/dates for docs + release notes.
